name: Parametric Printed SilkScreen w/ optional frame and squeegee

captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a 3D-printable silkscreen stencil with an integrated frame and an attached squeegee tool. The main body is a thin rectangular screen surrounded by a raised, thick boundary wall (the ink dam). The center of the screen features a stencil pattern in the shape of a question mark, which is rendered as a fine mesh of square grid holes. Extending from one short side of the frame is a flat squeegee blade with a chamfered scraping edge.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric silkscreen stencil generator in OpenSCAD. The design must feature a thin rectangular screen area with customizable dimensions, an optional raised ink-dam frame, a mesh grid pattern, and an optional squeegee tool with a beveled edge attached to one side. Include parameters to load a custom polygon path for the stencil image, define optional text, and adjust the grid spacing and thickness.
captions.factory: The script constructs the stencil by first defining a thin base sheet using a `cube` and subtracting the stencil pattern and text. The stencil pattern is generated by extruding a 2D `polygon` defined by an array of points using `linear_extrude`. A mesh screen is constructed by using nested `for` loops to generate thin, intersecting rectangular beams (`cube` primitives) across the screen area. The raised ink dam is built from four perimeter `cube` segments. Finally, the squeegee is generated on one side using `linear_extrude` on a 2D `polygon` that defines its beveled profile.
